events.text: Earliest cave art, radiocarbon dated to about 7300 BC (Group A).

events.label: occupation
events.text: Site is last inhabited, possibly by ancestors of the Tehuelche.

evidence.quote: The site was last inhabited around 700 AD
The site was last inhabited around 700 AD

events.text: Stylistic Group C (Rio Pinturas IV) begins, last cave art style.

events.label: first documentation
events.text: Father Alberto Maria de Agostini first writes about the site.

evidence.quote: first wrote about the site in 1941 AD

events.label: research
events.text: Carlos Gradin's team begins major research and excavation at the site.

evidence.quote: conducted the most important research on the site in 1964
conducted the most profound research on the site in 1964

events.label: heritage designation
events.text: Cueva de las Manos listed as a National Historic Site in Argentina.

evidence.quote: listed as a National Historic Site since 1993

events.label: heritage designation
events.text: Cueva de las Manos named a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

evidence.quote: listed as a World Heritage Site since 1999
its inclusion on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1999

undated_mentions: Art dated to a span between 11,000 and 7,000 BC (millennia-scale period)
Toldense people lived in the caves until the third or second millennium BC
Group B (new cultural group) born around 5,000 BC, with its art beginning before 5,000 BC
Group B/B1 cultural group activity ends around 1,300 BC
